blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from Jared's verified local notes (researched November 1, 2026). Listing-stated figures are labelled; unconfirmed items say so. No live feed filtered to 55+ homes yet.

In Abbotsford West, the 55+ homes you can buy are Evergreen Village, Elmwood Manor, Maplewood Manor, Heather Ridge and 13 more (strata, manufactured-home park and life lease). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is rental and retirement residence or care. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Abbotsford West

The sub-area's largest age-restricted strata: freehold strata plan NWS1737, built 1985, 205 units, 10 levels; the building directory records age restrictions, pets not allowed and rentals not allowed in its bylaws summary, with an indoor pool, recreation centre and workshop among the amenities. One listing feed has described rentals as allowed at this address — listings conflict, and under provincial law strata rental-restriction bylaws are void anyway; confirm the current registered bylaws before relying on either version.
Freehold strata NWS1317, built 1981; listings record a 55+ age restriction and no pets, with the strata fee covering electricity, heat and water.
Across from Elmwood Manor: 36 units, 3 storeys, built 1980, strata plan NWS1482; current listings describe it as a 55+ community.
21 units, 3 storeys, built 1979, strata plan NW1047; listings record 55+, no pets and no rentals.
Freehold strata, 3 levels, built 1987; a current listing records 55+, no pets and no smoking. Unit count: Not confirmed.

Strata plan NWS2756, built 1988, 3-level wood-frame building; listing data states the age restriction is 55 years and only one owner must be at least 55, rentals are allowed with certain restrictions, and pets and smoking are not allowed.
Listings describe a "desirable 55+ community" with no pets allowed. Year built and unit count: Not confirmed.
Freehold strata, plan NWS2196, built 1984; MLS property data records "Restricted Age: 55+".
A current listing describes "Clearbrook's desirable 55+ Fernwood Manor" with no pets allowed and the strata fee covering heat and hot water. Year built and unit count: Not confirmed.
Built 1993, gated townhouse/condo complex; listings record "Age 55+. No Pets.", that only one resident needs to be over 55, and that rentals to 55+ occupants are permitted.

Strata plan LMS1002; current MLS listing data records "Restricted Age: 55+", rentals allowed with restrictions and one cat welcome. An older building directory still describes this tower as 45+ with 55 units on 16 floors, built 1999 — that conflicts with current MLS data (which shows a 1994 build year) and with the post-2022 law; treat the directory entry as stale and verify the registered bylaw and Form B before relying on either.
A current listing calls it "one of Abbotsford's premiere age restricted communities," across from Mill Lake, with no pets allowed. Year built and unit count: Not confirmed.
Listings describe a "highly sought-after 55+ building" beside Mill Lake, with the strata fee covering gas, heat and hot water. Year built and unit count: Not confirmed.
Townhouse complex; listings record a 55+ age restriction, rentals allowed and pets not allowed. Year built is not confirmed (listings variously show 1984 and 1986).

Bare land strata, plan LMS2380, built 1996, 52 homes; a gated rancher-style community where listings record "Age Restricted 55+", pets allowed with restrictions and rentals allowed. MLS listing headings label this address Abbotsford West (postal code V4X 2R1) even though Downes Road reads as an east-side street — it is filed here on the MLS label.

Listings describe a "well maintained 55+ park" with a 55+ age restriction, and one small pet allowed with park approval. Homes here are manufactured homes on rented pads — the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act rules in apply, not strata law. Unit/site count: Not confirmed.
Life lease residences in Abbotsford West (an occupancy right, not strata)

Owned and operated by the non-profit Clearbrook Golden Age Society: a life lease residence for independent adults age 55 and over — residents pay an up-front Life Lease Capital Payment (typically the unit's BC Assessment value, per the Society) plus monthly maintenance charges, and get lifetime occupancy, not a strata title; the tower was completed in 1997 and holds 111 residential suites, and the building doubles as a community centre with a coffee shop, hair salon and hall rentals. The Society states there are typically no real estate fees or property transfer taxes on a life lease, and advises getting professional advice before signing one.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Abbotsford West (not for sale)

items.t: Tabor Manor — 31944 Sunrise Cres (Tabor Village campus): Independent living rental apartments: 38 rental apartments described by the operator as affordable; tenants can add services such as hairdressing, light housekeeping, food services and personal care. Rental only — nothing to buy.

Tabor Court — 31954 Sunrise Cres: Assisted living within the Tabor Village campus of care: 88 subsidized suites accessed through the Fraser Health Authority plus 16 privately rented suites, per the operator.

Tabor Home — 31944 Sunrise Cres: A 118-bed complex care facility; all beds are accessed through Fraser Health, with 24-hour nursing and a special care environment for residents with Alzheimer's and other dementias, per the operator. Registered with BC's Assisted Living Registry under operator Tabor Home Society.

MSA Manor — 2510 Gladwin Rd: Long-term care beside Mill Lake Park, run by the Maplewood Care Society: Fraser Health lists 34 publicly subsidized long-term care beds, all single-occupancy rooms; admissions are coordinated through Fraser Health, not by purchase or private application to the home.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Abbotsford West

items.t: "Abbotsford West" is the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board sub-area name used in board data; the City's own demographic geography calls the wider west side "West Abbotsford" (profile area 7) and treats Peardonville, Clearbrook, South Clearbrook and Townline as separate profile areas inside it — there is no single City neighbourhood plan named Abbotsford West.

Rough extent: Highway 1 across the north, Mt. Lehman Road and Clearbrook Road as the main north–south routes, South Fraser Way as the east–west arterial, and the Agricultural Land Reserve and Abbotsford International Airport (YXX) lands to the southwest. Precise sub-area edges are not published in text form by the City.
Central Abbotsford sits to the east, Aberdeen and Poplar to the west and northwest inside the city, Matsqui to the north, and Aldergrove (Township of Langley) to the west along Fraser Highway.

Where the 55+ stock actually is: it clusters in Clearbrook and around Mill Lake — Old Yale Road, Tims Avenue, Gladwin Road, Peardonville Road and Simon Avenue carry almost every verified age-restricted building in this sub-area. The Highstreet / Mt. Lehman end of the sub-area has no verified 55+ complex in any source checked.

Transit here is BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley system, not TransLink: routes 1 (Highstreet / UFV) and 2 (Highstreet / McMillan) run from Highstreet, route 66 Fraser Valley Express runs from Highstreet toward Lougheed Station, and the Highstreet Transit Exchange on Highstreet Access Road has six bus bays. There is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in Abbotsford.

Health anchors on the west side: Abbotsford Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 100-2692 Clearbrook Road (urgent care 9:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., seven days a week); the city's hospital, Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre at 32900 Marshall Road, sits just east in Central Abbotsford. Both are Fraser Health services.

School District 34 serves the area; catchments are set by SD34 Policy 18 and checked address by address in the district School Locator — locator runs show the west side splits (3614 Clearbrook Road returns Clearbrook Elementary → Colleen and Gordie Howe Middle → W.J. Mouat Secondary; 3433 Firhill Drive returns Blue Jay Elementary → Eugene Reimer Middle → Rick Hansen Secondary).

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Abbotsford West

items.t: 55+ is the only age bylaw a BC strata may have: Since Nov 24, 2022 (Bill 44), the Strata Property Act, ss. 123.1/123.2, allows a strata to restrict residents to 55 or older — and any older 19+, 40+ or 45+ bylaw stopped being enforceable that day. That is why the older 45+ description of Trethewey Tower cannot be relied on.
The bylaw governs who may live in the unit, not who may own it: The Province states that a person under 55 can own a strata lot in a 55+ corporation but may not be able to reside in it.

Exemptions are built into the law (Strata Property Regulation 7.01): people already living in the unit when the 55+ bylaw passed (legacy residents), live-in caregivers, and — expanded May 1, 2023 — a younger spouse or partner, children under 19 in the resident's care, and adult children the resident cared for before they turned 19.

No strata in BC can ban long-term rentals: Rental-restriction bylaws have been void province-wide since Nov 24, 2022, so where an older Abbotsford West listing says "no rentals," that bylaw no longer applies; a strata may still restrict short-term rentals, and a tenant in a 55+ building must still meet the age bylaw or an exemption.

Manufactured-home pads follow tenancy law, not strata law: The Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act covers most manufactured home tenancies in BC — the buyer owns the home and rents the site (as at Paradise Park). Pad rent can be increased only once every 12 months, with at least three full months' written notice, and the increase is capped at the provincial limit (2.3% for increases taking effect in 2026) plus a proportional amount for changes in local government levies and regulated utility fees.

City zoning already has a seniors-housing category: Abbotsford's Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 framework defines "Congregate Housing" — an independent living setting with common dining and amenity areas (definition added by Bylaw 3249-2022) — which is the use class the City's draft bylaw work associates with seniors supportive housing, assisted living and long-term care projects.

Suites in a house you already own: Zoning Bylaw s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings; City reports applying the bylaw state the criteria include a minimum 400 m² lot, 12.0 m frontage, not on a cul-de-sac bulb, and frontage on a Collector or Local road.

The governing plan is new: Abbotsforward 2050 is the City's Official Community Plan (Bylaw 2600-2016, as updated), and the current OCP document set (Bylaw No. 3690-2025) carries the vision that "people can stay in their neighbourhood as they age" — the policy hook for seniors housing proposals on the west side.
Property tax dates: City of Abbotsford taxes were due July 2, 2026; unpaid balances took a 5% penalty on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on September 16, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Abbotsford West

items.t: Almost all of Abbotsford's 55+ strata stock is in this one corridor. A buyer who insists on another part of Abbotsford is mostly choosing between detached houses, life lease, or rentals.

The two Tims Avenue buildings face each other and are not twins. Elmwood Manor (32025 Tims Ave, NWS1317, built 1981) and Maplewood Manor (32040 Tims Ave, NWS1482, built 1980) are separate strata corporations with separate bylaws and fees; Elmwood's listing data covers electricity, heat and water in the fee, which Maplewood's sources do not state.

Old directories still call Trethewey Tower 45+. A building directory in circulation describes 32440 Simon Ave as 45+; sub-55 age bylaws have been unenforceable since Nov 24, 2022, and current MLS data for the tower records "Restricted Age: 55+". Always price and qualify against the current registered bylaws, not a directory page.
Building data for the biggest 55+ building conflicts between sources. The directory figures are used in, but a buyer should reconcile against the strata plan and Form B before writing.

Downes Road Estates is filed "west" only because the MLS says so. The bare land strata at 32250 Downes Rd carries an Abbotsford West sub-area label in MLS listing headings (postal code V4X 2R1); a buyer searching by map alone would likely look for it in east-side results and miss it.

The City runs seniors programming out of the same Clearbrook corridor. The City's Abbotsford Seniors Connect Directory 2025–2026 lists Garden Park Tower / Clearbrook Golden Age Society among its seniors service profiles — the life lease tower at 2825 Clearbrook Rd doubles as a community centre open to non-residents, with a coffee shop and seniors programs.

Abbotsford's tax penalty is a two-step. Taxes were due July 2, 2026, with 5% added July 3 and a second 5% on September 16, 2026 — a buyer closing in late summer inherits whichever step has already landed on an unpaid balance.

faq.a: Yes for long-term tenancies: every strata rental-restriction bylaw in BC has been void since Nov 24, 2022, whatever the listing sheet or an old bylaw printout says. The tenant still has to satisfy the 55+ age bylaw or an exemption, and short-term rentals can still be banned by bylaw.
faq.q: A listing says "no rentals allowed." Can I actually rent my unit out?

faq.a: It is building-by-building on this side of town, and the 55+ buildings lean strict: Evergreen Village, Elmwood Manor, Heather Ridge, Silverwood Manor, Fernwood Manor, Centennial Court and Fircrest Estates all record no pets in listing/directory sources, while Downes Road Estates allows pets with restrictions, Trethewey Tower's current MLS data allows one cat, and Paradise Park allows one small pet with park approval. Confirm against the strata's registered bylaws or the park rules for the specific unit.

Tenure. Evergreen Village is freehold strata — you own the unit and can sell it on the open market. Garden Park Tower is life lease: an up-front capital payment (typically the BC Assessment value, per the Society) buys lifetime occupancy plus monthly maintenance charges, and on departure the Society redeems the lease under its terms — there is no strata lot to list.
faq.q: What's the difference between Garden Park Tower and a condo at Evergreen Village?

faq.a: The manufactured home itself. The pad is rented under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act: pad rent can rise only once a year, on at least three full months' notice, capped at the provincial limit (2.3% for 2026) plus the proportional levy/utility amount; resales in parks also run through the park's own approval process — the Paradise Park listing notes one small pet is allowed only with park approval, which shows the approval step is real.
faq.q: In Paradise Park, what do I actually own?

faq.a: Some do, per listing data: Elmwood Manor's fee is recorded as covering electricity, heat and water; Fernwood Manor's covers heat and hot water; Lakewood Gardens' covers gas, heat and hot water. That varies by building and by year — confirm the current fee inclusions on the Form B.
faq.q: Do any of the older buildings include utilities in the strata fee?

faq.a: Mechanically yes: the next buyer must be able to live there — 55+, an exempt spouse/partner, caregiver or legacy case — or buy without residing. That is the built-in trade-off of every BC 55+ strata since the 2022 changes confined age bylaws to 55+.
faq.q: Does the 55+ restriction shrink my resale market?

faq.a: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre is at 32900 Marshall Road, just east of this sub-area, and the Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 100-2692 Clearbrook Road. For regional transit, route 66 Fraser Valley Express runs from the Highstreet Transit Exchange toward Lougheed Station; Abbotsford's own buses are BC Transit, and there is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in the city.
faq.q: How do I get to the hospital and to Vancouver transit from Clearbrook?

faq.a: The Tabor Village campus on Sunrise Crescent stacks the ladder in one place: Tabor Manor's 38 independent rental apartments, Tabor Court's assisted living (88 Fraser Health-subsidized suites plus 16 private), and Tabor Home's 118 complex-care beds; MSA Manor adds 34 publicly subsidized long-term care beds on Gladwin Road, with admissions coordinated through Fraser Health.
